import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.BasisLinear
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.LineInPlaneCond
/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.
-/
lemma line_in_cubic_P_P_P! {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

/-- A `LinSol` satisfies `LineInCubicPerm` if all its permutations satisfy `lineInCubic`. -/
def LineInCubicPerm (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubic S`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := hS 1

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` for all permutations `M`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_permute {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) (M' : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group) :
    LineInCubicPerm ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M' S) := by
  rw [LineInCubicPerm]
  intro M
  change LineInCubic
    (((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M *
    (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M') S)
  erw [← (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep.map_mul M M']
  exact hS (M * M')

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

lemma P_P_P!_accCube' {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (f : Fin n.succ.succ → ℚ) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (hS : S.val = Pa f g) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P f) (P f) (basis!AsCharges (Fin.last n)) =
    - (S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) *
    (2 * S.val evenShiftLast +
    S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) := by
  rw [P_P_P!_accCube f (Fin.last n)]
  have h1 := Pa_evenShiftLast f g
  have h2 := Pa_evenShiftFst f g (Fin.last n)
  have h3 := Pa_evenShiftSnd f g (Fin.last n)
  simp only [Fin.succ_last, Nat.succ_eq_add_one] at h1 h2 h3
  have hl : f (Fin.succ (Fin.last n)) = - Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    simp_all only [Fin.succ_last, neg_neg]
  erw [hl] at h2
  have hg : g (Fin.last n) = Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    linear_combination -(1 * h2)
  have hll : f (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) =
      - (Pa f g (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))
      + Pa f g evenShiftLast) := by
    linear_combination h3 - 1 * hg
  rw [← hS] at hl hll
  rw [hl, hll]
  ring

lemma lineInCubicPerm_last_cond {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    LineInPlaneProp
    ((S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n))), ((S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))),
      (S.val evenShiftLast))) := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, hfg⟩ := span_basis S
  have h1 := lineInCubicPerm_swap LIC (Fin.last n) g f hfg
  rw [P_P_P!_accCube' g f hfg] at h1
  simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, neg_add_rev, mul_eq_zero] at h1
  cases h1 <;> rename_i h1
  · left
    linear_combination h1
  · cases h1 <;> rename_i h1
    · refine Or.inr (Or.inl ?_)
      linear_combination -(1 * h1)
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inr h1)

lemma lineInCubicPerm_last_perm {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInPlaneCond S := by
  refine @Prop_three (2 * n.succ.succ) LineInPlaneProp S
    (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))
    evenShiftLast ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · simp [Fin.ext_iff, evenShiftSnd, evenShiftFst]
  · simp [Fin.ext_iff, evenShiftSnd, evenShiftLast]
  · simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, evenShiftFst, evenShiftLast, Fin.isValue, ne_eq, Fin.ext_iff,
    Fin.coe_cast, Fin.coe_natAdd, Fin.coe_castAdd, Fin.val_last, Fin.val_eq_zero, add_zero,
    add_right_inj]
    omega
  · exact fun M => lineInCubicPerm_last_cond (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC M)

lemma lineInCubicPerm_constAbs {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).Sols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S.1.1) : ConstAbs S.val :=
  linesInPlane_constAbs_AF S (lineInCubicPerm_last_perm LIC)

theorem lineInCubicPerm_vectorLike {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).Sols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S.1.1) : VectorLikeEven S.val :=
  ConstAbs.boundary_value_even S.1.1 (lineInCubicPerm_constAbs LIC)

theorem lineInCubicPerm_in_plane (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).Sols)
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S.1.1) : ∃ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ.succ)).group),
    (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ.succ)).linSolRep M S.1.1
    ∈ Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range basis) := by exact?

/-- The permutations acting on the ACC system. -/
@[simp]
def FamilyPermutations (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemGroupAction (PureU1 n) where
  group := PermGroup n
  groupInst := inferInstance
  rep := permCharges
  linearInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberLinear] at i
    match i with
    | 0 => exact accGrav_invariant
  quadInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberQuadratic] at i
    exact Fin.elim0 i
  cubicInvariant := accCube_invariant

/-- The ACC system for a pure $U(1)$ gauge theory with $n$ fermions. -/
@[simps!]

    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep

  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h

  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

lemma P_P_P!_accCube' {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (f : Fin n.succ.succ → ℚ) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (hS : S.val = Pa f g) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P f) (P f) (basis!AsCharges (Fin.last n)) =
    - (S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) *
    (2 * S.val evenShiftLast +
    S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) := by
  rw [P_P_P!_accCube f (Fin.last n)]
  have h1 := Pa_evenShiftLast f g
  have h2 := Pa_evenShiftFst f g (Fin.last n)
  have h3 := Pa_evenShiftSnd f g (Fin.last n)
  simp only [Fin.succ_last, Nat.succ_eq_add_one] at h1 h2 h3
  have hl : f (Fin.succ (Fin.last n)) = - Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    simp_all only [Fin.succ_last, neg_neg]
  erw [hl] at h2
  have hg : g (Fin.last n) = Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    linear_combination -(1 * h2)
  have hll : f (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) =
      - (Pa f g (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))
      + Pa f g evenShiftLast) := by
    linear_combination h3 - 1 * hg
  rw [← hS] at hl hll
  rw [hl, hll]
  ring

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.BasisLinear
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.LineInPlaneCond
/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.
-/
lemma line_in_cubic_P_P_P! {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

/-- A `LinSol` satisfies `LineInCubicPerm` if all its permutations satisfy `lineInCubic`. -/
def LineInCubicPerm (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubic S`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := hS 1

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` for all permutations `M`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_permute {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) (M' : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group) :
    LineInCubicPerm ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M' S) := by
  rw [LineInCubicPerm]
  intro M
  change LineInCubic
    (((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M *
    (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M') S)
  erw [← (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep.map_mul M M']
  exact hS (M * M')

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2

    accCubeTriLinSymm (P f) (P f) (basis!AsCharges (Fin.last n)) =
    - (S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) *
    (2 * S.val evenShiftLast +
    S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) := by

  have h1 := Pa_evenShiftLast f g
  have h2 := Pa_evenShiftFst f g (Fin.last n)

  simp only [Fin.succ_last, Nat.succ_eq_add_one] at h1 h2 h3
  have hl : f (Fin.succ (Fin.last n)) = - Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    simp_all only [Fin.succ_last, neg_neg]
  erw [hl] at h2
  have hg : g (Fin.last n) = Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    linear_combination -(1 * h2)

      - (Pa f g (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))
      + Pa f g evenShiftLast) := by
    linear_combination h3 - 1 * hg
  rw [← hS] at hl hll
  rw [hl, hll]
  ring

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.BasisLinear
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.LineInPlaneCond
/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.
-/
lemma line_in_cubic_P_P_P! {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

/-- A `LinSol` satisfies `LineInCubicPerm` if all its permutations satisfy `lineInCubic`. -/
def LineInCubicPerm (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubic S`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := hS 1

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` for all permutations `M`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_permute {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) (M' : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group) :
    LineInCubicPerm ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M' S) := by
  rw [LineInCubicPerm]
  intro M
  change LineInCubic
    (((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M *
    (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M') S)
  erw [← (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep.map_mul M M']
  exact hS (M * M')

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

lemma P_P_P!_accCube' {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (f : Fin n.succ.succ → ℚ) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (hS : S.val = Pa f g) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P f) (P f) (basis!AsCharges (Fin.last n)) =
    - (S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) *
    (2 * S.val evenShiftLast +
    S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) := by
  rw [P_P_P!_accCube f (Fin.last n)]
  have h1 := Pa_evenShiftLast f g
  have h2 := Pa_evenShiftFst f g (Fin.last n)
  have h3 := Pa_evenShiftSnd f g (Fin.last n)
  simp only [Fin.succ_last, Nat.succ_eq_add_one] at h1 h2 h3
  have hl : f (Fin.succ (Fin.last n)) = - Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    simp_all only [Fin.succ_last, neg_neg]
  erw [hl] at h2
  have hg : g (Fin.last n) = Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    linear_combination -(1 * h2)
  have hll : f (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) =
      - (Pa f g (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))
      + Pa f g evenShiftLast) := by
    linear_combination h3 - 1 * hg
  rw [← hS] at hl hll
  rw [hl, hll]
  ring

lemma lineInCubicPerm_last_cond {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    LineInPlaneProp
    ((S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n))), ((S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))),
      (S.val evenShiftLast))) := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, hfg⟩ := span_basis S
  have h1 := lineInCubicPerm_swap LIC (Fin.last n) g f hfg
  rw [P_P_P!_accCube' g f hfg] at h1
  simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, neg_add_rev, mul_eq_zero] at h1
  cases h1 <;> rename_i h1
  · left
    linear_combination h1
  · cases h1 <;> rename_i h1
    · refine Or.inr (Or.inl ?_)
      linear_combination -(1 * h1)
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inr h1)

lemma lineInCubicPerm_last_perm {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInPlaneCond S := by
  refine @Prop_three (2 * n.succ.succ) LineInPlaneProp S
    (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))
    evenShiftLast ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · simp [Fin.ext_iff, evenShiftSnd, evenShiftFst]
  · simp [Fin.ext_iff, evenShiftSnd, evenShiftLast]
  · simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, evenShiftFst, evenShiftLast, Fin.isValue, ne_eq, Fin.ext_iff,
    Fin.coe_cast, Fin.coe_natAdd, Fin.coe_castAdd, Fin.val_last, Fin.val_eq_zero, add_zero,
    add_right_inj]
    omega
  · exact fun M => lineInCubicPerm_last_cond (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC M)

lemma lineInCubicPerm_constAbs {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).Sols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S.1.1) : ConstAbs S.val :=
  linesInPlane_constAbs_AF S (lineInCubicPerm_last_perm LIC)

theorem lineInCubicPerm_vectorLike {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).Sols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S.1.1) : VectorLikeEven S.val :=
  ConstAbs.boundary_value_even S.1.1 (lineInCubicPerm_constAbs LIC)

theorem boundary_value_even (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) (hs : ConstAbs S.val) :
    VectorLikeEven S.val := by
  have hS := And.intro (constAbs_sort hs) (sort_sorted S.val)
  intro i
  have h1 := ConstAbsSorted.AFL_even_below (sortAFL S) hS
  have h2 := ConstAbsSorted.AFL_even_above (sortAFL S) hS
  rw [sortAFL_val] at h1 h2
  rw [h1, h2]
  exact (InvolutiveNeg.neg_neg (sort S.val _)).symm

/-- A charge configuration for n even is vector like if when sorted the `i`th element
is equal to the negative of the `n + i`th element. -/
@[simp]
def VectorLikeEven (S : (PureU1 (2 * n)).Charges) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Fin n), (sort S) (Fin.cast (split_equal n) (Fin.castAdd n i))
  = - (sort S) (Fin.cast (split_equal n) (Fin.natAdd n i))

  numberLinear := 1
  linearACCs := fun i =>

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.
-/
lemma line_in_cubic_P_P_P! {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

/-- A `LinSol` satisfies `LineInCubicPerm` if all its permutations satisfy `lineInCubic`. -/
def LineInCubicPerm (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubic S`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := hS 1

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` for all permutations `M`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_permute {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) (M' : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group) :
    LineInCubicPerm ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M' S) := by
  rw [LineInCubicPerm]
  intro M
  change LineInCubic
    (((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M *
    (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M') S)
  erw [← (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep.map_mul M M']
  exact hS (M * M')

  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,

informal_proof:
To establish that for any `LIC : LineInCubicPerm S`, `LineInPlaneCond S` holds, we proceed methodically as follows:

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.BasisLinear
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.LineInPlaneCond
/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.
-/
lemma line_in_cubic_P_P_P! {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

/-- A `LinSol` satisfies `LineInCubicPerm` if all its permutations satisfy `lineInCubic`. -/
def LineInCubicPerm (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubic S`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := hS 1

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` for all permutations `M`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_permute {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) (M' : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group) :
    LineInCubicPerm ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M' S) := by
  rw [LineInCubicPerm]
  intro M
  change LineInCubic
    (((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M *
    (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M') S)
  erw [← (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep.map_mul M M']
  exact hS (M * M')

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

lemma P_P_P!_accCube' {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (f : Fin n.succ.succ → ℚ) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (hS : S.val = Pa f g) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P f) (P f) (basis!AsCharges (Fin.last n)) =
    - (S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) *
    (2 * S.val evenShiftLast +
    S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) := by
  rw [P_P_P!_accCube f (Fin.last n)]
  have h1 := Pa_evenShiftLast f g
  have h2 := Pa_evenShiftFst f g (Fin.last n)
  have h3 := Pa_evenShiftSnd f g (Fin.last n)
  simp only [Fin.succ_last, Nat.succ_eq_add_one] at h1 h2 h3
  have hl : f (Fin.succ (Fin.last n)) = - Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    simp_all only [Fin.succ_last, neg_neg]
  erw [hl] at h2
  have hg : g (Fin.last n) = Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    linear_combination -(1 * h2)
  have hll : f (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) =
      - (Pa f g (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))
      + Pa f g evenShiftLast) := by
    linear_combination h3 - 1 * hg
  rw [← hS] at hl hll
  rw [hl, hll]
  ring

lemma lineInCubicPerm_last_cond {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    LineInPlaneProp
    ((S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n))), ((S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))),
      (S.val evenShiftLast))) := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, hfg⟩ := span_basis S
  have h1 := lineInCubicPerm_swap LIC (Fin.last n) g f hfg
  rw [P_P_P!_accCube' g f hfg] at h1
  simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, neg_add_rev, mul_eq_zero] at h1
  cases h1 <;> rename_i h1
  · left
    linear_combination h1
  · cases h1 <;> rename_i h1
    · refine Or.inr (Or.inl ?_)
      linear_combination -(1 * h1)
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inr h1)

lemma lineInCubicPerm_last_perm {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInPlaneCond S := by
  exact?

/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.
-/
lemma line_in_cubic_P_P_P! {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

/-- A `LinSol` satisfies `LineInCubicPerm` if all its permutations satisfy `lineInCubic`. -/
def LineInCubicPerm (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubic S`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := hS 1

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` for all permutations `M`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_permute {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) (M' : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group) :
    LineInCubicPerm ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M' S) := by
  rw [LineInCubicPerm]
  intro M
  change LineInCubic
    (((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M *
    (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M') S)
  erw [← (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep.map_mul M M']
  exact hS (M * M')

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

lemma P_P_P!_accCube' {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (f : Fin n.succ.succ → ℚ) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (hS : S.val = Pa f g) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P f) (P f) (basis!AsCharges (Fin.last n)) =
    - (S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) *
    (2 * S.val evenShiftLast +
    S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) := by
  rw [P_P_P!_accCube f (Fin.last n)]
  have h1 := Pa_evenShiftLast f g
  have h2 := Pa_evenShiftFst f g (Fin.last n)
  have h3 := Pa_evenShiftSnd f g (Fin.last n)
  simp only [Fin.succ_last, Nat.succ_eq_add_one] at h1 h2 h3
  have hl : f (Fin.succ (Fin.last n)) = - Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    simp_all only [Fin.succ_last, neg_neg]
  erw [hl] at h2
  have hg : g (Fin.last n) = Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g evenShiftLast := by
    linear_combination -(1 * h2)
  have hll : f (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) =
      - (Pa f g (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + Pa f g (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))
      + Pa f g evenShiftLast) := by
    linear_combination h3 - 1 * hg
  rw [← hS] at hl hll
  rw [hl, hll]
  ring

lemma lineInCubicPerm_last_cond {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    LineInPlaneProp
    ((S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n))), ((S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))),

if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of

namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1

a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,

  intro g f hS

    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

  intro M

    (((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M *
    (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M') S)
  erw [← (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep.map_mul M M']
  exact hS (M * M')

    - (S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) *
    (2 * S.val evenShiftLast +
    S.val (evenShiftSnd (Fin.last n)) + S.val (evenShiftFst (Fin.last n))) := by

Returns the successor of the argument.

The bound in the result type is increased:
```
(2 : Fin 3).succ = (3 : Fin 4)
```
This differs from addition, which wraps around:
```
(2 : Fin 3) + 1 = (0 : Fin 3)
```

    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by

  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.

  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

First, we fix an arbitrary index \( j \) and define a new permuted cubic structure \( S' \) by swapping the even-shifting of \( g \) and \( f \). This operation does not change the essential properties of the cubic structure we're examining, as it only reorders the elements in a specific way.

Next, we utilize the fact that after this permutation, the representation of the structure in the new basis, \( S' \), maintains the linearity inherent to cubic permutations. This is justified by the properties of the permuted basis and the fact that linearity is preserved under permutation operations.

We then apply the lemma 'line_in_cubic_P_P_P!', which ensures that certain invariants hold true within the permuted structure \( S' \). Specifically, these invariants guarantee that the expression \( (S'.\text{val}(j, j, j) - S'(j, j, j)) \) evaluates to zero, as the subtraction cancels out the identical components introduced by the permutation.

Finally, by combining these results, we conclude that the entire expression \( (S'.\text{val}(j, j, j) - S'(j, j, j)) \times \text{accCubeTriLinSymm}(P(g), P(g), \text{basis}!.\text{AsCharges}(j)) \) must indeed be zero.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.BasisLinear
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.LineInPlaneCond
/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.
-/
lemma line_in_cubic_P_P_P! {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

/-- A `LinSol` satisfies `LineInCubicPerm` if all its permutations satisfy `lineInCubic`. -/
def LineInCubicPerm (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubic S`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := hS 1

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` for all permutations `M`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_permute {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) (M' : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group) :
    LineInCubicPerm ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M' S) := by
  rw [LineInCubicPerm]
  intro M
  change LineInCubic

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.BasisLinear
import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.LineInPlaneCond
/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.
-/
lemma line_in_cubic_P_P_P! {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

/-- A `LinSol` satisfies `LineInCubicPerm` if all its permutations satisfy `lineInCubic`. -/
def LineInCubicPerm (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubic S`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := hS 1

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` for all permutations `M`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_permute {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) (M' : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group) :
    LineInCubicPerm ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M' S) := by
  rw [LineInCubicPerm]
  intro M
  change LineInCubic
    (((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M *
    (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M') S)
  erw [← (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep.map_mul M M']
  exact hS (M * M')

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

/-- The permutation which swaps i and j. -/
def pairSwap {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) : (FamilyPermutations n).group where
  toFun s :=
    if s = i then
        j
    else
      if s = j then
        i
      else
        s
  invFun s :=
    if s = i then
        j
    else
      if s = j then
        i
      else
        s
  left_inv s := by
    aesop
  right_inv s := by
    aesop

informal_proof:
To establish the statement, we proceed as follows:

1. **Assumption**: We begin by assuming that the set `S` satisfies the condition `lineInCubicPerm S`. This means that all lines in the set `S` adhere to the specific cubic permutation criteria defined by `lineInCubicPerm`.

2. **Application of Permutation `M`**: Consider a permutation `M` applied to `S`, resulting in the set `M S`. Permutation `M` rearranges the elements of `S` according to the rules dictated by the permutation group `FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)`.

3. **Line Transformation**: Each line in `M S` is obtained by applying the permutation `M` to the corresponding elements in `S`. Since permutations merely rearrange elements without altering their inherent properties, applying `M` to a line in `S` should maintain the structural integrity of the line with respect to the cubic permutation criteria.

4. **Closure Under Permutation**: Given that `S` satisfies `lineInCubicPerm`, and `M` represents a valid permutation within the group `FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)`, the permuted set `M S` must also satisfy `lineInCubicPerm`. This follows from the fact that permutations preserve the essential properties required for a line to be classified as satisfying the cubic permutation condition.

5. **Conclusion**: Hence, for any permutation `M`, if `lineInCubicPerm S` holds, then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` must also hold, thereby proving that the condition is preserved under arbitrary permutations of the set `S`.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.LineInPlaneCond
/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,

    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := hS 1

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubicPerm (M S)` for all permutations `M`. -/

/-- The permutations acting on the ACC system. -/
@[simp]
def FamilyPermutations (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemGroupAction (PureU1 n) where
  group := PermGroup n
  groupInst := inferInstance
  rep := permCharges
  linearInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberLinear] at i
    match i with
    | 0 => exact accGrav_invariant
  quadInvariant := by
    intro i
    simp only [PureU1_numberQuadratic] at i
    exact Fin.elim0 i
  cubicInvariant := accCube_invariant

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.LineInPlaneCond
/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

/--
This lemma states that for a given `S` of type `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear` and
a proof `h` that the line through `S` lies on a cubic curve,
for any functions `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ` and `f : Fin n → ℚ`, if `S.val = P g + P! f`,
then `accCubeTriLinSymm.toFun (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`.
-/
lemma line_in_cubic_P_P_P! {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS
  linear_combination 2 / 3 * (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 1) -
    (lineInCubic_expand h g f hS 1 2) / 6

/-- A `LinSol` satisfies `LineInCubicPerm` if all its permutations satisfy `lineInCubic`. -/
def LineInCubicPerm (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
  LineInCubic ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S)

/-- If `lineInCubicPerm S` then `lineInCubic S`. -/
lemma lineInCubicPerm_self {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (hS : LineInCubicPerm S) : LineInCubic S := by exact?

informal_statement: For a function defined on the line through a point $S$ lying on a cubic curve, the mixed partial derivatives with respect to the variables $g$ and $f$ exhibit a symmetry property. Specifically, the mixed partial derivative with respect to $g$ twice and $f$ once is equal to half the mixed partial derivative with respect to $g$ once and $f$ twice.
informal_proof:
Given a function defined on the line through a point \( S \) lying on a cubic curve, we aim to demonstrate the symmetry of mixed partial derivatives. Consider variables \( g \) and \( f \) and their respective projections \( P_g \) and \( P_f! \). We start by expressing the first fundamental structure functions in terms of these projections:

\[
\begin{cases}
P_g = \alpha_1 X_1 + \beta_1 Y_1 + \gamma_1 Z_1, \\
P_f! = \alpha_2 X_2 + \beta_2 Y_2 + \gamma_2 Z_2.
\end{cases}
\]

Taking the second partial derivatives of \( P_g \) and substituting the resulting expression into the first equation, we find that the second fundamental structure functions are also expressible in terms of these projections. Specifically, we have:

\[
\frac{\partial^2 P_g}{\partial g^2 \partial f} = \alpha_1 \frac{\partial X_1}{\partial g \partial f} + \beta_1 \frac{\partial Y_1}{\partial g \partial f} + \gamma_1 \frac{\partial Z_1}{\partial g \partial f},
\]

\[
\frac{\partial^2 P_g}{\partial g \partial f^2} = \alpha_2 \frac{\partial X_2}{\partial g \partial f} + \beta_2 \frac{\partial Y_2}{\partial g \partial f} + \gamma_2 \frac{\partial Z_2}{\partial g \partial f}.
\]

By leveraging the properties of the cubic curve and the symmetry of the mixed partial derivatives, we establish that:

\[
C_1^{21} = C_2^{12}.
\]

Applying this result back to our original expressions for the first and second fundamental structure functions, we find that the mixed partial derivatives satisfy the desired symmetry:

\[
\frac{\partial^2}{\partial g^2 \partial f} = \frac{1}{2} \frac{\partial^2}{\partial g \partial f^2}.
\]

Thus, we have proven that the mixed partial derivatives exhibit symmetry, as required.

    τ.toCubic (S + T) = τ.toCubic S +

informal_statement: A line lying on two planes, which pass through a given point, is entirely contained within a cubic surface if and only if every point on the line satisfies the cubic equation defining the surface.
informal_proof:
To prove this statement, we consider a line that lies on two distinct planes, both passing through a common point $P$. Since the line is the intersection of these two planes, any point on the line can be expressed as a linear combination of points from each plane.

Let us denote the two planes as $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$, and let $Q$ and $R$ be points on $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$, respectively. Then, any point $S$ on the line can be written as $S = Q + t(R - Q)$, where $t$ is a scalar parameter. Since both $Q$ and $R$ lie on their respective planes, which pass through $P$, the parameterization of $S$ inherently satisfies the conditions of the planes.

Substituting the expression for $S$ into the cubic equation $ax^3 + by^3 + cz^3 + \dots = 0$ (representing the cubic surface), we observe that due to the linearity of the planes and the polynomial nature of the cubic equation, the combination will always result in a value that satisfies the equation. 

Under normal circumstances, substituting a linear combination into a cubic equation would generally yield a cubic polynomial in terms of $t$. However, since the line lies entirely on the cubic surface, this polynomial must simplify to zero for all values of $t$, ensuring that every point on the line satisfies the cubic equation.

Therefore, the line is entirely contained within the cubic surface, confirming that the property holds true.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.LineInPlaneCond
/-!

# Line In Cubic Even case

We say that a linear solution satisfies the `lineInCubic` property
if the line through that point and through the two different planes formed by the basis of
`LinSols` lies in the cubic.

We show that for a solution all its permutations satisfy this property, then there exists
a permutation for which it lies in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis.

The main reference for this file is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf
-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- A property on `LinSols`, satisfied if every point on the line between the two planes
in the basis through that point is in the cubic. -/
def LineInCubic (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
  accCube (2 * n.succ) (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0
annotation:

C1_dependencies.name: PureU1.accCube
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The cubic anomaly equation. -/
@[simp]
def accCube (n : ℕ) : HomogeneousCubic ((PureU1Charges n).Charges) :=
  (accCubeTriLinSymm).toCubic

C1_dependencies.name: PureU1
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The ACC system for a pure $U(1)$ gauge theory with $n$ fermions. -/
@[simps!]
def PureU1 (n : ℕ) : ACCSystem where
  numberLinear := 1
  linearACCs := fun i =>
    match i with
    | 0 => PureU1.accGrav n
  numberQuadratic := 0
  quadraticACCs := Fin.elim0
  cubicACC := PureU1.accCube n
